newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes weaken as margins swing negative.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes weaken as margins swing negative.

text.p: Asian crude prices were weaker on Friday with most pressure centred on light Middle East grades, traders said.
They were talked and offered at much lower levels for March loading than outgoing premiums on February trading -- largely as a result of reduced Japanese and South Korea demand.
Murban was offered at more than ADNOC +30 cents, although others put the market at a wider +35 to +50. The crude was last traded in February at +80 cents.
A major was awarded the monthly Kenya tender earlier this month for Murban at ADNOC +52 cents.
Qatar Land deals were heard around QGPC +26 cents, although one was also heard at QGPC +42 cents, but was said to involve a major selling to an affiliate.
Umm Shaif, which earlier this week traded at ADNOC +35 cents, was talked between +30 and +40 cents.
Dubai spreads came in as refineries bought crack spreads. Refinery margins are under pressure and Shell confirmed it has cut Singapore runs to 95 percent.
March/April Dubai came in to 38/42 cents per barrel from a day-earlier 45/47 cents. Topping margins on Arab Light were $1 negative and just a few cents negative on Dubai feedstock.
